text: How the Master has cut down Daughter Zion from the skies, dashed Israel's glorious city to earth, in his anger treated his favorite as throwaway junk.
Raging, he smashed Judah's defenses, made hash of her king and princes.
broke Israel's arm and turned his back just as the enemy approached, came on Jacob like a wildfire from every direction.
and killed our young men, our pride and joy. His anger, like fire, burned down the homes in Zion.
He chewed up and spit out all the defenses. He left Daughter Judah moaning and groaning.
God wiped out Zion's memories of feast days and Sabbaths, angrily sacked king and priest alike.
and turned the fortifications over to the enemy. As they cheered in God's Temple, you'd have thought it was a feast day!
He assembled his crew, set to work and went at it. Total demolition! The stones wept!
her kings and princes off to exile—no one left to instruct or lead; her prophets useless—they neither saw nor heard anything from God.
They throw dust on their heads, dress in rough penitential burlap— the young virgins of Jerusalem, their faces creased with the dirt.
My insides have turned to jelly over my people's fate. Babies and children are fainting all over the place,
then fainting like dying soldiers in the streets, breathing their last in their mothers' laps.
What can I say to give you comfort, dear Zion? Who can put you together again? This bust-up is past understanding.
They didn't face you with your sin so that you could repent. Their sermons were all wishful thinking, deceptive illusions.
They rub their eyes, they shake their heads over Jerusalem. Is this the city voted "Most Beautiful" and "Best Place to Live"?
Then they rub their hands in glee: "We've got them! We've been waiting for this! Here it is!"
He always said he'd do this. Now he's done it—torn the place down. He's let your enemies walk all over you, declared them world champions!
Let the tears roll like a river, day and night, and keep at it—no time-outs. Keep those tears flowing!
Pour your heart out face to face with the Master. Lift high your hands. Beg for the lives of your children who are starving to death out on the streets.
Should women eat their own babies, the very children they raised? Should priests and prophets be murdered in the Master's own Sanctuary?
my young men and women killed in their prime. Angry, you killed them in cold blood, cut them down without mercy.
so that on the big day of God's wrath no one would get away. The children I loved and reared—gone, gone, gone."
